I played this with 3 friends and had the time of my life. This game is just fun. There's really no other way to describe it.

Pros:
Customisation - Balls can be customised to a colour and the lobby host can change the physics of the game by changing the ball shape, gravity, bounce height, toggling collisions with other players, etc. Makes for a laugh with low gravity, bouncy eggs.
Simplicity - The game is simple with a minimalist art style, runs on pretty much any machine very well. Do note that 'Medium' and 'High' settings have their FPS capped, where as 'low' is uncapped.
Fun - Just, fun. Like a game should be.
Affordable - Definitely worth the price, an absolute blast to play.

Cons:
Maps - only two maps at the moment, however these are very cool. I especially like the Oasis map as it has some really cool features like the river section.

Dear devs:

Please add workshop compatibility later in development, it would be awesome to have the community make custom maps, also please make more maps of your own as I love the level design currently in game!

Overall verdict:
Fun, easy to run, affordable - get it, especially if you like mini golf.

I understand that this game was probably someone's college project but jeez louise is it buggy. The fundamentals for a mini-golf game would be 1. consistent physics, 2. consistent collision with objects and 3. consistent positioning of balls when the same shot is played. This game fails on all 3 of these and it ruins what could be a really fun game to play with your friends.

It's almost impossible to go through an 18 hole course without encountering one (or most likely many) of the following:
- hitting an invisible wall
- getting reset unnecessarily
- going through a solid object
- having your starting position different to others

I keep playing it hoping to get through a game without having any bugs but it's just not possible.

Somehow this game is simultaneously a really fun game and the worst game I have ever played. Nothing on the face of the planet brings out my rage like a round of Gold with your Friends and after every session I vow to never play this game again, but somehow I keep coming back.

This game is pretty fun to play with friends. It doesn't offer anything revolutionary as far as golf games go, but the mechanics and the visuals are solid, and the different maps, gameplay options, and workshop content offers a lot of replayability.

The main downside to this game is it's a bit unstable. My friends and I have encountered quite a few bugs, including crashes, disconnects, graphical issues, golf balls getting stuck or becoming impossible to hit, etc. It seems to have gotten better since the game fully released, but the issues haven't gone away completely. However, my friends and I are used to this at this point, and the strange issues we sometimes encounter just add to the experience and give us something else to yell about, so this hasn't been a huge deal for us.

TL;DR Despite some issues with stability, this game's solid mechanics and replayability make this a fun game that is worth picking up if you've got some friends to rage with.

The physics are janky as hell, especially in water and on steep slopes/loops. Some levels are literally impossible in hockey mode, not to mention the completely random movements of the goalies. Dunk mode is stupid. The music is mostly grating and repetitive. And the 12 stroke + 2 minute limit applies to ALL levels regardless of size or complexity.

Golf with your friends is a great game to play with a group of people you know while talking on teamspeak or something. You may run out of friends though if you turn on collisions.

Golf With Your Friends is one of those games that looks simple at first glance but quickly proves how chaotic, clever, and endlessly replayable it can be. On the surface, it’s a colorful mini-golf game where players try to sink a ball into a hole in as few strokes as possible. In practice, it’s a fast-paced multiplayer experience that thrives on unpredictability, friendly competition, and absolute nonsense—in the best way possible. The fun does not stop there, golf with friends have made sure you can play endless amount of different maps, which makes the average player enjoy the game for an even longer period of time. The addition of cheap DLC's gives a new perspective to ingame purchas'. I would recommend this title for others to play from now on and forward.

Very few games have made me rage and laugh. While the game can be a bit infuriating, I must admit that the game is enjoyable. The map designs can be very creative and colorful. The best maps are just tough enough to pose a challenge, but leave you feeling a sense of satisfaction and pride. It takes some getting accustomed to the power levels and the cameras can make things difficult by leaving you viewing at odd angles. The worst is when you somehow end up off the green and in a tight place that the game says is playable despite being stuck.
All of these, while annoying, can be fixed with the press of a button. As the name says, the game is best enjoyed with friends. I feel it is best to play with two or three other people. Together, you can all rave about the game, lightly poke fun at one another over terrible strokes, or just relax and enjoy a conversation over some golf. I would highly recommend the game. I give it a 9/10.

The netcode of the game leaves something to be desired however, but that is the only flaw I can think of. Doesn't break the game but does break immersion when you see other people's balls not moving like you would expect them to.

Great game, but the latest update has caused an ongoing problem of invisible obstacles that can only be seen in the free cam view. This is even a problem on maps that were made my the developers themselves. This problem has made the game pretty much unplayable and if it's left unaddressed, will undoubtedly kill the game. I loved this game so much but I can't continue to play if the problem is going to persist.
